images.filename: Hull City in the Premier League - geograph.org.uk - 817803.jpg
images.caption: Hull City in the Premier League Hull City.... Premier League? String those two phrases together and it sounds a bit like comedian Peter Kay's "Garlic Bread" routine. Nevertheless the 104 year old football club has finally achieved what to many seemed impossible. Until two days ago, Hull had the unenviable distinction of being the largest conurbation in England never to have had a football team compete in the top division. Thanks to a spectacular goal by 39 year old Hull-born striker Dean Windass in the playoff final at Wembley, that dubious honour now passes to Plymouth. The picture is of crowds outside Ferens Art Gallery in Victoria Square trying to catch a glimpse of the players as they appear on the City Hall balcony.

images.filename: Ferens Art Gallery at Night - geograph.org.uk - 1560622.jpg
images.caption: Ferens Art Gallery at Night Ferens Art Gallery is situated in Victoria square in Hull.  The area is illuminated by high pressure sodium lighting which gives rise to this weird effect.  Superficially, it looks as though the square was deserted, but the long exposure has 'lost' the people as none were standing still at the time!

images.caption: Fountain in Princes Quay Princes Quay is a shopping complex in the centre of Hull and is built on 'stilts' above the former Princes Dock.  There are two fountains in the dock now and this is the most northerly one.  The shopping centre itself can be seen in the background.  The photograph was taken with an exposure time of about six seconds to give this effect.
